title: MAX_RANK_INCREASE split: loop guards 1024 (Rust/C) vs 2048 (constants.toml, C wire default, Python dodag); no stack reads constants.toml (R-RPL-002, draft 5.1-adjacent)
description:
Spec/appendix: appendix-rpl claims 'All constants from constants.toml [rpl]'; draft 5.1 table says MAX_RANK_INCREASE 1024. Appendix-rpl sweep R-RPL-002, divergent, confidence high.
Evidence (verified this sweep): constants.toml:52 max_rank_increase = 2048; Rust loop guard MAX_RANK_INCREASE: u16 = 1024 (rust/lichen-rpl/src/dodag.rs:28, used :119-142,281); C Kconfig default 1024 (lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl/Kconfig:111-118) but C DODAG-Configuration wire default 2048 (messages.c:604); Python constants.py:51 = 1024 while python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py:50 = 2048 (the RPL module uses its own 2048). Wire default is 2048 in all three DIO-config builders (Rust message.rs:680-681, Py messages.py:104, C messages.c:604). The cross-stack admission divergence is documented as a risk in test/vectors/ccp_beacon_sig_gate.json:140-150 ('divergence_risk: max_rank_increase_default'). Also: constants.toml header claims Rust include_str!/C generated constants.h/Python lichen.constants — none machine-read it (all hand-synced; grep-verified).
Suggested placement: pick one value (1024 per draft+Rust/C loop guards, or 2048 per toml+wire default), align all guards + wire defaults + ccp_beacon_sig_gate.json divergence note, and decide whether constants.toml should become actually machine-read (header currently overclaims).
